headline: Multiancestry methods extend variant association mapping to cell types and deep models
label: Multiancestry Genetic Variant Mapping
summary: Ancestry-diverse and cell-type-resolved datasets now test whether eQTL, fine-mapping, and sequence models generalize beyond European bulk-tissue settings.
synthesis: The common thread is moving association mapping beyond single-ancestry, bulk-tissue settings. traceCB integrates single-cell and bulk eQTL summary statistics across ancestries to recover cell-type-specific effects. A MAGENTA benchmark evaluates Borzoi and AlphaGenome on multi-ancestry blood eQTLs, finding that these sequence-to-function models only weakly match nominal effects but better separate high-PIP fine-mapped variants. MIFM groups variants by LD under a multiple-instance objective to train a deep sequence classifier that predicts causal regulatory variants. On the trait side, a multiancestry GWAS meta-analysis of lung cancer (87 loci) yields PRS-MAMT, a multiancestry, multitrait polygenic score validated across European and Asian cohorts. What is new is the combination of ancestry diversity, cell-type resolution, and learned regulatory prioritization within a single analytic framework.
